content_voiceover: Let's wrap up with high-yield points specific to Taiwan. The most common irregular red cell antibodies here are anti-Mia and anti-E, different from Western populations where anti-K tends to dominate. That's because antigen prevalence differs, Mia positivity in Taiwan is about seven percent, and E antigen positivity is around fifty percent, both much higher than in Caucasian populations. Next, severe transfusion reactions with respiratory distress point to two classic mimickers, TACO and TRALI, distinguishing them is a frequent board question. There's also transfusion-associated graft-versus-host disease, know its prevention, at-risk populations, and clinical features, including a rise in pro-BNP. Finally, some TRALI cases are caused by donor anti-leukocyte antibodies, so blood centers now preferentially use male donors for plasma products, since males lack pregnancy-related HLA sensitization, a policy Taiwan implemented in 2015.
keypoints: Most common irregular antibodies in Taiwan: anti-Mia and anti-E
Mia positivity about 7.3%; E antigen positivity about 50% in Taiwan
Severe dyspnea after transfusion: think TACO versus TRALI
TRALI can be caused by donor anti-leukocyte antibodies
Taiwan uses male-only plasma donors since 2015 to reduce TRALI risk
